knowledge_units.context_summary: A series of star-shaped aromatic nitric acid radicals were synthesized via demethylation and oxidation of phenolic precursors, exhibiting high stability and nonradiative decay suitable for photothermal conversion. The specific material TPA-TPA-O6 demonstrated a water evaporation efficiency of 89.41% and a rate of 1.293 kg/m² h under one sunlight, representing top performance among pure organic small molecule photothermal materials.

These materials are synthesized via demethylation and oxidation of phenolic precursors and exhibit high thermal, electrochemical, and light stability. The specific compound TPA-TPA-O6 demonstrates superior photothermal conversion efficiency and water evaporation performance compared to other organic small molecules.

HOMO energy levels were determined via cyclic voltammetry for four specific radical compounds.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study characterizes star-shaped aromatic nitric acid radicals (ANARs) using ESR, UV-Vis, and PLQY measurements, finding that high spin concentration correlates with enhanced nonradiative decay and photothermal efficiency. TPA-TPA-O6 exhibits superior broadband absorption and photothermal performance compared to triazine and pyrene-core analogs due to stronger donor-acceptor conjugation. The materials were tested for solar-driven water evaporation, with TPA-TPA-O6 showing high efficiency and stability.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study evaluates the solar-driven water evaporation performance of TPA-TPA-O6 loaded in polyurethane foam, achieving high efficiency and rate under one-sun illumination. The material demonstrates superior solubility and reproducibility compared to inorganic counterparts and facilitates seawater desalination by reducing primary ion concentrations. TPA-TPA-O6 is highlighted for its low-cost synthesis, high yield, and competitive photothermal conversion properties among organic materials.
